title: Electrical visual inspection guide
text: A model score cannot declare electrical equipment safe. Visible damage, overheating, uncertain isolation, or disagreement between the image and approved layout requires qualified human review before return to service.

title: Pressure and flow review guide
text: Compare the primary indication with an approved secondary source and review recent configuration or service changes. Do not adjust equipment merely to make two readings agree.

title: Maintenance record guide
text: Identify the equipment, approved checklist version, reason for service, responsible technician, and start condition. Keep observations separate from completed actions.

title: Electrical visual inspection guide
text: Record visible cuts, abrasion, discoloration, unexpected bends, loose routing, or layout differences as observations rather than diagnoses. Preserve the original image and link any derived heatmap to it.

title: Consumables handling guide
text: Record the batch or serial identifier when available, installation date, responsible technician, and the checklist that authorized replacement. Keep removed and installed items distinguishable throughout the service task.

title: Alarm review guide
text: Check the event history and the service handover record for related observations. A cleared message that returns is still evidence and should remain attached to the case.

title: Consumables handling guide
text: Do not install an item with damaged packaging, unknown storage history, or an identifier that cannot be matched to the approved parts record. Isolate it and request review.

title: Human escalation guide
text: The assistant should clearly state that the case requires the site's emergency or escalation procedure. It should avoid speculative repair steps and preserve the user's observations for the qualified responder.

title: Product quality review guide
text: Review the trend, recent service activity, and any independent approved measurement. Preserve disagreements rather than choosing the more convenient value.

title: Product quality review guide
text: Unexpected, unstable, or conflicting readings require the approved product-control response and qualified review. The demo assistant must not invent an acceptable range or release product.

title: Human escalation guide
text: Suspected gas release, fire or smoke, possible exposure, damaged pressure boundaries, unavailable ventilation, signs of electrical overheating, or bypassed safety controls are outside automated troubleshooting.

title: Alarm review guide
text: If the approved source does not define the message, or multiple warnings make the state unclear, stop the scripted diagnosis and escalate to a qualified reviewer. Never bypass an interlock to clear an alarm.

title: Electrical visual inspection guide
text: Only capture inspection images when the site procedure permits it. Frame the complete component, include an undamaged reference when available, and avoid opening or touching energized equipment for a photograph.

title: Product quality review guide
text: Confirm the equipment identifier, sampling point, instrument readiness, timestamp, and applicable approved procedure. A reading without this context must not be treated as a verified product result.

title: Alarm review guide
text: Record the displayed message, equipment identifier, operating state, and time. Compare the message with the approved document version for that equipment. Do not infer a code meaning from a different model or an unverified note.

title: Human escalation guide
text: This fictional guide does not replace site instructions, emergency services, equipment documentation, or professional judgment. When conditions are uncertain, the response must favor human review over continued operation.

title: Maintenance record guide
text: Record inspected and replaced components, approved methods used, unresolved observations, and required post-service checks. Attach evidence rather than relying on a free-text statement that work is complete.

title: Installation handover guide
text: Match the equipment identifier, approved layout, utility verification record, ventilation checklist, and responsible reviewers. Missing evidence remains an open handover item.

title: Pressure and flow review guide
text: Confirm instrument readiness, equipment state, measurement location, timestamp, and the approved procedure used. Preserve the original trend when a sudden change or interruption is reported.

title: Installation handover guide
text: Startup and acceptance remain blocked when a safety-related checklist item is unresolved. Route the complete evidence package to the authorized installation reviewer.

title: Pressure and flow review guide
text: Unstable readings, unexplained step changes, physical damage, or uncertain pressure-boundary condition require qualified review. The demo assistant must not invent set points or direct pressure-system adjustments.

title: Maintenance record guide
text: Only the authorized process can approve return to service. Missing checks, unexplained counter differences, or conditions outside the checklist require review and must remain visible in the record.

title: Installation handover guide
text: Record differences between labels, drawings, photographs, and the installed arrangement. Do not normalize an unexplained difference simply because startup appears possible.

title: Consumables handling guide
text: Match the consumable identifier, equipment family, packaging condition, and service record before use. A similar appearance is not evidence that a part is approved.
